style.name: Warm Oilcloth Family
style.style_notes: Paint each creature as something loved: broad, flat color, sincere eyes and a slight wobble in the edge. Keep marks few and steady between frames. Dark paint belongs inside the creature; the surrounding cell stays clear. Glass keeps its clear heart and soft rim, while ink gives solid bodies their weight. Warmth comes from care, not a shine added to everything.
style.framing: Use transparent 192 × 208 cells. Keep every pose inside x=16–176 and y=16–192, with standing feet or body base at y=184. Reserve room above for jumps and beside the body for waves. Fit tall creatures by gently bending their posture, keeping their defining shape. Lock scale, face placement and carried objects across frames. Each row has 16 frames at 8 fps: two seconds, four beats of four frames. Repeat held drawings within that grid. Keep motion within the cell; movement across the screen belongs to the player. One-shot rows finish in a stable pose. Idle and waiting use small movements and long holds.
style.palette: Core paint: soot #262321, cream #F1DFC1, ochre #C59A46, rust #AC5740, herb green #65764C and blue #557589. Preserve each seed's own colors: the trolleybus stays blue, the ram gold, the ermine white and the droplet clear. Lights stay within their existing flame, lantern, window or body. V2 adds sixteen selectable looks to the base sheet, each covering all nine rows and all twenty seeds. These change paint handling and small accents, never creature, costume or props: 1. Dry Paint—sparse broad grain; 2. Full Paint—solid matte fills; 3. Thin Paint—slightly translucent fills; 4. Broken Edge—small fixed gaps in solid-body outlines; 5. Soft Edge—gentler edge transitions; 6. Firm Edge—clearer shape boundaries; 7. Cream Edge—a narrow light-facing rim; 8. Soot Edge—a deeper inward border; 9. Ochre Touch—ochre on existing small accents; 10. Rust Touch—rust on existing small accents; 11. Herb Touch—green on existing small accents; 12. Blue Touch—blue on existing small accents; 13. Pale Paint—lighter secondary colors; 14. Deep Paint—darker secondary colors; 15. Quiet Paint—less saturated secondary colors; 16. Fresh Paint—stronger secondary colors. Protect identity colors and face contrast in every look. Glass variants affect rim softness, tint or inner light only; its center remains clear.
style.line: Solid bodies use irregular ink edges about 3 pixels wide, with essential inner marks at least 2 pixels wide. Keep important gaps at least 4 pixels open. Suggest texture with a few broad marks fixed to the body, never changing noise. The glass droplet is the deliberate exception: use a broad, soft, partly open rim and a clear center, without a hard black enclosure. The magnifying glass has an ink frame and a clear lens. Family likeness comes from shared proportions, restraint and timing, rather than forcing glass to become opaque ink.
style.boundaries: All twenty seeds remain themselves. Keep the magnifying glass's raised eyebrow and searching tilt; the ram's gold fleece, herb sprig and attached twig that greens with happiness; the hut's chicken legs, kerchief roof and door broom; the sleepy mushroom's moss, tarragon and herb basket; the crescent's lantern; the still white ermine's distinct frost crown; the bold calf's embroidered felt blanket and hoof stamp; the book's flapping covers and changing ink pictures; the determined brush's legs and paint jar; the thoughtful inkpot's spectacles and tucked quill; the quiet palette's paint spots and brush tail; the curled lamb's striped cap and candle; the calm clear droplet; the gentle giraffe's long neck and sincere eyes; the precise bee's white collar and pressed flower; the generous pomegranate's opening rind and visible seeds; the courteous wooden soldier's back key and salute; the tuning fork's poised turns; the blue trolleybus's warm windows and guitar visible on its seat; and the clay lamp's grapevine handle. Use new poses, markings and patterns. Existing belongings remain attached, held or securely contained. Do not add shared herbs, keys, lamps, costumes or ornaments to other seeds. Sweeping leaves no footprint marks; frost appears only on the crown or feet; underlining and writing become small gestures without drawn words; shared seeds stay cupped in the open rind. Humming and ringing read through posture without sound symbols. No floating effects, scene background, text, speech bubbles, shadows or new review props. Review uses only the creature and its existing belongings. All pets and sheets remain local. Paul waived approval steps and retains a later veto.

rows.idle: Beat 1: settled pose. Beat 2: one slow blink or slight head dip. Beat 3: a 1–2 pixel breath. Beat 4: return and hold. Keep sleepy pets curled, proud pets upright and the palette quietly seated. Loop gently.
rows.running-right: Face right. Beat 1: first contact. Beat 2: lift and pass. Beat 3: opposite contact. Beat 4: lift and return. Legs stride, wheels turn, covers or bee wings beat; legless bodies tip and bob along the same pulse. Keep carried objects secure.
rows.running-left: Use the same four-beat travel cycle facing left. Redraw the turn so the eyebrow, herbs, quill, broom, guitar and other uneven details remain attached to their proper places. Do not simply mirror the finished sheet.
rows.waving: Beat 1: turn toward the viewer. Beat 2: raise an available limb, cover, branch or body edge. Beat 3: make one clear greeting sweep. Beat 4: lower and settle. Bodies without limbs tilt in greeting. Keep held flames and jars upright. Play once.
rows.jumping: Beat 1: crouch or compress. Beat 2: rise 10–14 pixels. Beat 3: reach the peak and descend. Beat 4: land, soften and settle. Winged pets use a brief upward flap; the trolleybus gives a small springy hop. Show no trails or landing marks. Play once.
rows.failed: Beat 1: stop abruptly. Beat 2: sink or tilt downward. Beat 3: hold a plainly disappointed pose. Beat 4: recover slightly while keeping the lowered gaze. No damage or comic panic. Play once and hold; this must differ from a sleepy idle.
rows.waiting: Beat 1: look toward the expected action. Beat 2: hold. Beat 3: make one restrained questioning tilt or weight shift. Beat 4: hold with eyes open. The calf may make one small hoof press. Existing lights stay steady. Loop without pacing.
rows.running: This means a task is active, not travel. Stay planted and lean toward the work. Beat 1: prepare. Beat 2: act. Beat 3: check. Beat 4: reset. The hut sweeps close to its feet, the brush works at its own jar rim, the inkpot traces an empty underline gesture, the book turns a pictured page and the magnifier scans. Other seeds use focused body motions with their existing belongings. Loop.
rows.review: Beat 1: become still and attentive. Beat 2: inspect an existing body detail or belonging, or turn thoughtfully when there is none. Beat 3: hold the considered pose. Beat 4: give one small nod and settle. The magnifier angles its lens inward; the palette studies a paint dab. Keep the motion small and distinct from the broad greeting. Add nothing. Play once.

style.why: I want each pet to look cared for, with its own work and temper still visible. The dark oilcloth feeling lives in the painted body and can meet a dark app surface without baking a background into the sprite. No veto is proposed. Originality may veto only in a jury and never ranks taste. The Painter checks function at native size across all nine rows and sixteen added looks. Any function flag must name the pet, look, row and frame, and describe visible evidence such as a vanished eyebrow, a clipped crown or two actions with the same silhouette. These are checks to perform, not defects claimed without images. Any later charter veto must quote the exact guards-against line and give a concrete reason.

brief.description: A kind golden ram whose patient care brings green leaves to an attached dry twig.
brief.brief:
Medea is a small golden ram with soft fleece the color of old gold, steady eyes and a fresh herb sprig held securely at one corner of her mouth. Short curled horns frame a confident face. A dry twig nestles firmly in the fleece over her shoulder, where its shape remains visible beside her head. Her magic has a clear, modest result: when happiness arrives, attached buds open into green leaves, one after another.

She is generous, capable and quietly proud. She greets with an offered forehoof, waits with open attention and meets a setback with lowered ears before gathering herself. Her warmth comes from deliberate gestures and sincere eyes. Broad ochre paint, cream fleece marks, herb green leaves and irregular soot edges give her weight; a few fixed light patches suggest old gold without glitter.

Her signature behavior is a pause to notice new growth, followed by a small satisfied lift of the chin. Focused work uses a planted stance and a forehoof to gather the mouth-held herb stems neatly together. Review instead turns her head over her shoulder to inspect the attached twig. These actions must read through the whole pose at native size.

Keep her belongings secure and her renewal gentle. Leaves remain attached; resetting a loop must never depict withering. Give her no costume, extra tools, floating effects or scene dressing.
brief.pet_notes: A compact ram with a rounded gold fleece body, short sturdy legs, cream muzzle and small ochre curled horns. Kind dark eyes sit clear of the horn curls. The herb sprig stays at her left mouth corner; the attached twig rises from her right shoulder fleece. Use broad matte paint, slightly uneven soot edges and a few fixed cream marks, with open gaps around hooves, horns and leaves.

rows.idle: Across 6 frames, stand evenly with relaxed ears, blink once, breathe gently and return to a settled hold while the sprig and twig stay quiet.
rows.running-right: Across 8 frames, face right and cycle through alternating hoof contacts and lifted passes, keeping the mouth-held sprig and shoulder twig secure.
rows.running-left: Across 8 frames, redraw the left-facing stride with the sprig and twig on their proper body sides, preserving the same steady travel rhythm.
rows.waving: Across 4 frames, turn toward the viewer, raise the free right forehoof, sweep it once in greeting and lower it into a stable stance.
rows.jumping: Across 5 frames, crouch, rise, reach a compact airborne peak, land softly and settle with every belonging attached.
rows.failed: Across 8 frames, stop, lower the chest and ears, hold a disappointed downward gaze and recover slightly into a stable lowered pose without damage or leaf loss.
rows.waiting: Across 6 frames, keep the chest upright and eyes open toward the expected action, extend the head slightly, make one questioning ear tilt and hold without handling the herbs.
rows.running: Across 6 frames, stay planted, lean forward, lift the left forehoof beneath the mouth-held stems, gather them together, check their alignment and reset the hoof for another careful pass.
rows.review: Across 6 frames, plant all four hooves, turn the head back toward the shoulder twig, follow its attached buds opening into leaves, hold the inspection and give a small satisfied nod before settling.

do_not_resemble: No franchise look-alike, logo, real-person likeness or copied artwork.
brief.why: This draft makes renewal visible through attached leaf growth and gives care a concrete action. I assume the sprig is mouth-held and place the twig at the right shoulder so inspection remains readable. Leaf growth finishes in a stable leafy pose; any later dry starting state is a separate state reset, never an animated loss of growth. The v2 contract overrides the sheet's conflicting frame and look instructions: one local transparent 1536 × 2288 atlas, eight columns by eleven rows, with 192 × 208 cells; rows 0–8 contain 6, 8, 8, 4, 5, 8, 6, 6 and 6 frames respectively, and unused cells remain fully transparent. Retain the sheet's 8 fps as a timing assumption, using held drawings within those counts. Keep poses within x=16–176 and y=16–192, with standing feet at y=184 and consistent scale and facial construction. Rows 9 and 10 contain single gaze/pose directions, not paint variants: row 9 is 000, 022.5, 045, 067.5, 090, 112.5, 135, 157.5; row 10 is 180, 202.5, 225, 247.5, 270, 292.5, 315, 337.5, clockwise with 000 up. Preserve one palette and treatment, separating neighboring directions through muzzle, horn and ear placement, especially row 10 frames 5–7. The supplied readability notes guide distinct silhouettes: relaxed idle, upright outward waiting, forward hoof-and-herb work, and backward twig inspection. Carry these distinctions into every later image prompt. No images were supplied for this draft, so I claim no new measured function defects; later flags must identify pet, direction or base look, row, frame and visible evidence. Motion measurements are guidance recorded in provenance, and only skill validators gate production. Review adds no props; all rows exclude floating effects, backgrounds, text, speech bubbles and shadows. No veto is proposed, and Originality has no taste-ranking role. Paul waived approval and retains a later veto; all assets remain local.
